overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law as alleged: April 26 minutes were inaccurate and incomplete, May 10 minutes omitted a change order document, and the May 10 notice topic was insufficiently specific; the hygienist report and notice-documentation claims failed, and the April 26 notice claim was untimely.

allegations.summary: April 26 minutes allegedly recorded several votes inaccurately and omitted documents used at the meeting; the Board amended them.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that the minutes of the April 26 meeting were inaccurate and insufficient in the ways alleged.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 26 meeting notice was insufficiently specific; filed too late, so the AG declined to review it.
allegations.key_passage: Because the April 26 meeting occurred in open session, any allegation about the sufficiency of the notice for that meeting should have been filed on or before May 26.

allegations.summary: May 10 minutes failed to list a change order document used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that the minutes of its May 10 meeting did not specifically list a change order document that was used at the meeting.

allegations.summary: May 10 minutes allegedly omitted a hygienist's asbestos report used at the meeting; Board said the information was shared verbally, not as a document.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Board was not required to list this report in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Notices allegedly lacked supporting documentation and documents were not posted before meetings.
May 10 notice topic '10 Pleasant Street Change Order' was allegedly too vague to inform the public of the asbestos removal discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic “10 Pleasant Street Change Order” was insufficient to inform the public that the Board would discuss removal of asbestos from the demolition project at the listed property.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no additional remedial action because the minutes were already amended).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
